question: Does public-source discovery provide fish taxa or site-resolved sampling from the Matandang Sabang River Watershed, and is the announced watershed assessment a useful primary-source retrieval lead?

searches: "Matandang Sabang River Watershed" fish OR ichthyofauna OR species survey
"Watershed Characterization and Vulnerability Assessment" "Matandang Sabang" PDF
method.directSourceAccess: The DENR CALABARZON article returned HTTP 403 when opened directly. Its indexed text was reviewed, and the same announcement was available in a DENR CALABARZON newsletter PDF mirror. The complete WCVA report, annexes, and underlying data were not located or retrieved.
boundaries: No account, request, email, form, or download was initiated.
A neighboring Tayabas Bay fisheries assessment was checked only to prevent transfer of landing-site catch data into this freshwater watershed.
Search results about mangrove flora, user-generated fishing pages, and unrelated waters were not treated as fish-survey evidence.

findings.denrAnnouncement: DENR CALABARZON reports that GRIDS and DENR-CENRO Catanauan presented Watershed Characterization and Vulnerability Assessment results for the Matandang Sabang River Watershed on 8 October 2025. The announcement says the assessment area encompasses Catanauan, General Luna, Buenavista, and Lopez, Quezon, and covers physical, biological, socioeconomic, and environmental topics.
findings.fishEvidence: The public summary supplies no fish names, station or waterbody sampling table, field dates, fish-sampling methods, identification or voucher details, full report, or reuse terms. The broad statement that biological characteristics were assessed does not establish that fish were sampled.
findings.adjacentMarineSource: The existing NFRDI Tayabas Bay assessment reports 2004-2013 fishery landing surveys including Matandang Sabang Kanluran and Masaka in Catanauan, but it aggregates and raises catch data to the bay. Landing location does not establish freshwater capture origin or river occurrence; no data were transferred.
findings.scope: The new research lead records the exact announced watershed name and four-municipality study-area description. It does not assert a river course, watershed boundary, fish presence, salinity, safety, or catchability.

interpretation.sourceValue: The DENR announcement is a useful lead to request the complete primary assessment and any biological or aquatic appendices; it is not itself a fish checklist.
interpretation.dataModelBoundary: Keep this multi-municipality watershed lead separate from Catanauan River, Tayabas Bay landing records, and individual aquatic sampling stations until a primary source establishes their relationship.
interpretation.rightsBoundary: Do not reproduce report tables, images, taxa, or derived data until the exact report/data access and reuse conditions are clarified.

disposition.nextAction: If Joseph chooses, send the separate unsent draft to the appropriate DENR-CENRO Catanauan or GRIDS contact after confirming the official recipient. Meanwhile continue public-source discovery for dated, site-resolved fish surveys across Quezon freshwater sites.

sources.supports: Announcement of the WCVA presentation, its 8 October 2025 event date, the named study area, and four-municipality coverage; not fish taxa or sampling results.
Existing adjacent marine-bay landing-assessment source considered as a non-transferable catch-data boundary.
